payload.query: Does the 10 lakh cumulative Capital Market figure in UPI OC185B make a single IPO mandate limit 10 lakh?

claims.text: The 10 lakh figure in UPI OC185B represents a cumulative limit for the Capital Market category over 24 hours, not a single IPO mandate limit.

The ₹10 lakh cumulative limit for Capital Market transactions (MCC 6211) is established under Circular 185B, not as a specific mandate limit for single IPOs. The rule regarding the enhanced per-transaction limit of ₹5 lakh for Retail Direct Scheme and UPI-based ASBA IPOs is explicitly stated in Circular 127.

claims.text: Circular OC 186A introduces UPI Tap & Pay on Point of Sale (PoS) terminals as an additional mode for initiating UPI transactions via Near Field Communication (NFC), extending the feature beyond QR codes to enable contactless payments by tapping unlocked mobile devices.
UPI Tap & Pay on PoS terminals shall be accepted only for Person-to-Merchant (P2M) transactions.
Payee PSPs must enable UPI Tap & Pay exclusively on NFC-enabled PoS terminals certified in accordance with PCI PTS / CPOC standards.
UPI Application Providers and PSP Banks must obtain explicit user consent after each device binding operation before allowing further UPI Tap & Pay transactions.
Members and UPI Application Providers must obtain explicit user consent for enabling the UPI Tap & Pay feature, while ensuring users retain the ability to opt out at any time.
Payee PSPs are required to integrate the Point-of-Sale Common Library for UPI (PoS CL) on all PoS terminals within their acquiring network.
UPI Application Providers must ensure device lock is enabled as a prerequisite for activating UPI Tap & Pay, and the device must be unlocked at the time of initiating a transaction.

Remitter Banks must validate the user's account for UPI Tap & Pay feature enablement status before processing each transaction, and users may set their own transaction limits within the ceiling of ₹5000.
UPI Application Providers must present UPI Tap & Pay as a standalone feature via a dedicated call-to-action, without embedding it within other services or menu categories.
